text.tspan: We can now combine these two potentials together, and this captures both the effect of the
polymer and of the short-range capillary force on the position of the two beads. It also
gives us an equation of motion, the Langevin equation, that lets us simulate this polymer
and study its dynamics. From there, we can compute the distributions of time the polymer
spends open and closed. The dynamics of a Rouse polymer usually is not Markovian,
however we assumed that these opening and closing durations were independent.
This lets us compute the likelihood of a trajectory, and therefore, the Fisher information.
